idiom_name: document (property map + child documents) plus one typed view per concern
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: model the data as a map from keys to values, plus child documents under child keys, and expose it through a single document contract (get, put, children). Attach behaviour by declaring one narrow view interface per concern — a trait — implemented in terms of get/put with the keys that concern owns, and give concrete noun types no state beyond the document they were constructed over, so several views share one map. Traversal must go through a caller-supplied constructor so each child is wrapped in the right view instead of being handed out as a raw map. Keep keys in shared constants, validate that required properties are present and correctly typed where the document enters the system, and decide up front whether the document is immutable (wrap the inner map in an unmodifiable view) or mutable with explicit ownership rules.
code_sketch:
document = map(key -> value) + map(key -> list<document>)
put(key, value); get(key); children(key, make_view)
view HasModel(doc):  model() = cast<string>(doc.get("model"))
view HasPrice(doc):  price() = cast<number>(doc.get("price"))
noun Car(doc) : HasModel, HasPrice      # views share one document
car = Car(document_from(json)); car.model()  # typed access, no field copies
pitfalls: Wrong move: scatter raw string keys at call sites -> failure: a typo creates a missing or empty view and the compiler cannot find it -> instead: namespace each key in the owning view and use shared constants or enum members.

Wrong move: copy the property map when constructing a view -> failure: writes and sibling readers diverge from the original document -> instead: keep one shared map reference, or explicitly choose an immutable snapshot and prohibit writes.

Wrong move: let arbitrary subsystems put values without validation -> failure: the wrong type survives the write and throws deep in a later accessor -> instead: validate at the ingress factory and expose typed setters for owned keys.

Wrong move: treat typed views and raw get/put as interchangeable -> failure: business logic becomes stringly typed and bypasses the view contracts -> instead: keep generic operations inside the document layer and publish view methods to callers.

Wrong move: let independent views reuse an unnamespaced key -> failure: one plugin silently overwrites another plugin's value -> instead: namespace key constants and reject collisions when extensions register.

Wrong move: cast a numeric value to a narrower runtime type (for example, Long to Integer) -> failure: ClassCastException appears at the read site -> instead: normalise to the declared type at ingress or perform an intentional Number conversion.
Wrong move: hand out the underlying map -> failure: callers mutate it without invariants and create a second untyped code path -> instead: expose read-only traversal or controlled view access.

Wrong move: claim immutable views while the backing map or child list remains mutable -> failure: callers mutate the tree behind the view -> instead: wrap every map and child collection or enforce an immutable document contract.

Wrong move: treat a missing key as equivalent to an explicit null -> failure: defaults and required-property checks become ambiguous -> instead: model presence separately and validate required keys at the boundary.
Wrong move: cache child views across document replacement -> failure: accessors read stale maps after a reload -> instead: rebuild views from current child maps or make document identity immutable.

Wrong move: accept unknown keys without an ownership or version policy -> failure: schema drift and collisions remain latent until production -> instead: preserve unknown data while registering namespaces and migrating or defaulting keys at ingress.
